submission.justification:
Radiator-R3 at 3 cm thickness achieves the best pion/kaon separation performance with a sigma of 4.685, representing a 22.4% advantage over Radiator-R1 (best sigma: 3.826) and a 52.5% advantage over Radiator-R2 (best sigma: 3.073). 

A comprehensive simulation campaign was conducted, testing all three radiator candidates at six thickness points (1-6 cm in 1 cm steps, totaling 18 simulations). Radiator-R3 demonstrated superior performance across most thickness values and achieved its peak separation at 3 cm, which falls well within the allowed thickness constraint of 1-6 cm.

The performance advantage is substantial and consistent with the physics expectations for RICH detectors: R3's higher refractive index generates more Cherenkov photons, leading to better angular resolution and improved particle identification. While long-term stability considerations exist for aerogel radiators, standard mitigation strategies (such as dry nitrogen purging) can maintain performance over the experiment's lifetime.

This recommendation optimizes the primary goal of achieving the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c while satisfying all constraints.
